summary: UNODC guidelines specifically tailored for the health-care sector to detect wrongdoing, mitigate corruption risks, and protect whistleblowers, with a focus on supply chain integrity and emergency response.
sector_vulnerabilities: Medical product supply chain (falsified drugs/medical supplies).
Public procurement of large-scale medical equipment and services.
Health insurance fraud and billing abuse.
Intermediaries in international medical supply markets (amplified during COVID-19).

policy_pillars.focus: Establishment of internal, open, and inclusive reporting channels with accessible interfaces.
Legal and administrative safeguards against retaliation; provision of support and feedback to reporting persons.
Confidentiality and anonymity as core requirements for trusted reporting systems.

operational_impact: Detection of corruption at an early stage in the health sector is recognized as a life-saving measure, preventing harm from low-quality or falsified medical products.
